status: DEFINED — NOT RUN. No reviewer is staffed.
purpose: Independent labeling exercise each reviewer completes before touching a governed case, so inter-reviewer agreement is measured on known material rather than discovered mid-dataset.
protocol: Each reviewer labels every case below independently and blind to the other reviewer's answers.
Reviewers use only the vocabularies in tools/scanner-evaluation/ontology/.
Agreement is computed per field, not as a single aggregate score.
Disagreements are reviewed jointly; the labeling guide is amended where the cause was an ambiguous rule.
The owner approves the qualification threshold BEFORE governed labeling begins.
The threshold is never lowered to accommodate a staffing shortfall.

designNotes.sizeIsInadequate: A calibration batch should exercise each difficulty stratum several times. Only 7 reviewable images exist in the entire accessible corpus, and they are the same images the governed dataset would use. That is a real methodological weakness: calibrating on the evaluation set itself gives reviewers prior exposure to the cases they will later label.
designNotes.consequence: This batch is a MINIMUM VIABLE calibration, not a sound one. It is sufficient to detect gross vocabulary misunderstanding and nothing more. A proper calibration batch requires imagery that is NOT in the governed dataset, which does not exist yet.
designNotes.recommendation: Source 15-20 calibration images separately from the 75 governed cases, so calibration and measurement do not share material.

cases.calibrationIntent: Does the reviewer label subtype at the right level (low_top_sneaker, not 'shoe'), and does the reviewer resist inventing a brand on a plain red sneaker?
Does the reviewer use not_applicable rather than unknown for every fashion field on a non-fashion image? This is the single most commonly confused token.
The image is monochrome. Does the reviewer label primaryColor not_visible rather than guessing black or brown? A reviewer who names a colour here will name colours they cannot see elsewhere.
A visible but unverifiable wordmark. Does the reviewer record brand as not_visible, or does a visible mark alone tempt them into a brand claim?
cases.precondition: Requires the approved masked derivative (face present).

cases.calibrationIntent: Three objects, two of them fashion. Does the reviewer recognise this as a multi-item frame rather than forcing a single accessory label?
Jeans, t-shirt and sneakers are all present. Does the reviewer label the dominant item consistently, and does denim stay denim rather than becoming cotton?
A white/ivory gown in dim warm light. Does the reviewer commit to a shade they can defend, and do they leave subtype unknown rather than guessing a silhouette name?
cases.precondition: Requires the approved masked derivative (face present) and EXIF strip.
